bull.b: The combination of no debt, meaningful liquidity and an estimated multi-year runway gives Streamex time to develop its tokenized-gold platform without immediate refinancing pressure. This financial flexibility can support partnerships, integrations and product scaling while limiting dependence on near-term capital markets.

The sharp sequential reduction in expenses and losses indicates management is actively resetting the cost base as commercialization begins. If these savings persist, lower fixed spending should extend liquidity, reduce the revenue required for breakeven and improve operating leverage as platform activity grows.

Completing the custody, attestation, brokerage and liquidity stack addresses important access requirements for institutional users. These relationships can strengthen product credibility and distribution, creating a foundation for broader adoption of tokenized gold if prospective holders complete diligence and allocations.

bear.b: Streamex continues to consume cash despite recent cost reductions, leaving the business reliant on existing liquidity and funding outside operations. Sustained negative cash generation can constrain investment choices and shorten the runway if revenue growth or expense reductions do not develop as management expects.

The platform has demonstrated initial activity, but externally held assets and recurring revenue remain small relative to the company’s operating needs. Dependence on a forthcoming institutional allocation makes scaling execution-sensitive, while limited current adoption provides little evidence yet of durable commercial traction.

The Nasdaq deficiency creates an ongoing corporate and execution burden over the next several months, with a possible reverse split or eventual delisting process if compliance is not restored. Listing uncertainty can complicate investor access and management’s ability to maintain market support while the business scales.
